answer: The registry makes agent identity expensive by binding each new agent to a bonded stake, slashed whenever two registrations share one proof-of-work lineage. A newcomer solves the miner challenge and locks collateral; the ledger keeps seed ancestry, so a farmer spawning thousands of wallets finds every one inheriting the same narrow basalt root and pays the full bond again. With the bond in real tokens and duplicate roots triggering a comet-shaped cascade of slashes, cloning identities costs more than one honest agent earns. That spiral of compounding stake makes sybil sprawl self-defeating.
